is_the_failure_to_fire_a_DEFECT_IN_THE_C.answer: A DEFECT IN THE CONTROL'S FIT WINDOW, not a real property of the object, and NOT a defect in the tolerance.
is_the_failure_to_fire_a_DEFECT_IN_THE_C.why: the 5-point fit that fails spans rho0 = 10, which is pre-asymptotic: for BOTH bases the 5-point and tail-3 exponents differ by ~1.5-3x more than the two bases differ from each other on the tail. On the window the gate actually uses everywhere else (tail-3, rho0 >= 100) the two bases agree to 5.4e-05, i.e. 185x inside the pre-committed tolerance, and BOTH tail-3 exponents are within 1e-3 of zero (C4: -6.180e-05, quintic C2: -7.718e-06). The object -- the exponent -- is basis-independent. The control mis-specified its own window.
is_the_failure_to_fire_a_DEFECT_IN_THE_C.what_it_does_NOT_change: NOTHING. The gate's exponent, the NO, and every number in item 1 are computed on the tail-3 window and are unaffected.

does_anything_the_NO_rests_on_depend_on_.the_constant: c_mod IS basis-dependent. constant_ratio_curl_C4_over_C2quintic = 1.476038407975093 -- the degree-9 C4 smoothstep gives a c_mod 47.6% larger than leg 381's quintic C2 smoothstep. The reported 869.288 per unit similarity time is therefore a BASIS-DEPENDENT number as well as a profile-dependent one (CORRECTIONS.md SS34 already records the profile dependence; the BASIS dependence is recorded here for the first time).
